tagline: A diamond of highways through ground that keeps turning up bones.
intro: From Grand Junction the loop runs west to Fruita and turns north on Highway 139 over Douglas Pass, 8,205 feet up in the Book Cliffs, down to Rangely and on to the town of Dinosaur and the Utah line. It goes on west through Vernal and Duchesne, over a pass to Helper and Price, south to Green River and Moab, and up to Cisco and the interstate east.

Colorado's byway page calls the ground fractured and stained. It gives up bones. Near Price there is a prehistoric museum and the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry, an old Jurassic mud trap, and the loop reaches both the Green and the Colorado.

moments.title: Fruita
moments.text: Each May the town holds a festival for Mike, a chicken who lived 18 months after his head was cut off and went on tour as a sideshow.

moments.title: Dinosaur Quarry
moments.text: North of Jensen a hall stands over the Wall of Bones, a rock layer tilted 67 degrees with thousands of fossils in it, where Earl Douglass found Apatosaurus vertebrae in 1909.

moments.title: Castle Gate
moments.text: Two sheer sandstone walls stand either side of the Price River like a gate. At the depot here in 1897 Butch Cassidy and Elzy Lay made off with $7,000 in coal company gold.

practical: Services are limited on some stretches.
